newsitem.title: USA: Calif. schools receive $180 mln in lottery funds.
newsitem.headline: Calif. schools receive $180 mln in lottery funds.

text.p: Over $180 million of lottery revenues were tranferred to California's public schools in the first three months of the fiscal year, state Lottery officials said on Tuesday.
Lottery sales for the July through September period reached $493 million, officials said. By law, the lottery must transfer at least 34 percent of its annual sales to public education.

Since 1985, the California lottery has raised more than $8.4 billion for public schools and has provided an annual average of approximately 38 percent of total revenues to schools, lottery officials said.
Lottery revenues are transferred quarterly to local school boards and the governing bodies of the statewide California State University and University of California systems.
The 1996-1997 fiscal year for the California lottery began on July 1, 1996.
